_source: Transcribed from the Kaggle log of notebook 07-zeroshot-2d-detection, version 2 ('FEAS-002 GPU zero-shot all 7 stations', GPU T4 x2, 665.1 s, 2026-11-14). Gallery pictures are screenshots of the notebook figures; summary.json, detections.csv, views/*.jpg and pred/*.npz are in the Output tab of that version.

detections_by_predicted_class.Damper: 6 detections, 0 correct (all are round recessed ceiling lamps)
detections_by_predicted_class.Exit sign: 21, 0 correct (all are red EXTINCTEUR / fire-safety signs, a FRANCE sign)
detections_by_predicted_class.Outlet: 134, 24 correct (wrong ones are switches and red manual fire call points)
detections_by_predicted_class.Switch: 50, 9 correct (wrong ones: green exit signs, door number plates, EXTINCTEUR signs, notice boards)

diagnosis: Grounding DINO finds the small wall devices (localisation good) but names them wrongly: switches -> 'outlet', green exit signs -> 'switch', red call points (part of Fire terminal) -> 'outlet', downlights -> 'smoke detector', red extinguisher signs -> 'exit sign'. With the per-point argmax a switch detected as outlet (0.41) beats the correct switch detection (0.30). Smoke detectors were never proposed. Three of seven stations had no tripod disc (views from the floor centre).
decision: Zero-shot naming is not good enough; zero-shot proposals are useful. Next: class-agnostic proposals + a few-shot classifier on our labelled objects (DINOv2 crop features, leave-one-station-out) + 3D context (height above floor, wall/ceiling, size); better scanner-position estimate for S164/S168/S178/S179.
